title: Candidate Prioritization Scorer and Onboarding Acceleration Kit
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working doc proposes a lightweight candidate prioritization scorer to help recruiters + hiring managers quickly triage candidate pools and a companion onboarding acceleration kit that gets new hires to first-impact in 30 days. Intended for fast-growing teams and roles where speed-to-offer and ramp time materially affect product timelines (e.g., infra, serving runtime, devtools).

Status and approach:
- Draft: shared for feedback with hiring managers and TA partners (Marco, Sofia invited).
- Goal: reduce screening backlog by 40% and standardize first-30-day expectations across eng and product hires.
- Must be usable in Google Drive and as a one-click export to Greenhouse or Lever.

1) Candidate Prioritization Scorer (one-pager usage)
- Inputs: resume signal, coding/technical exercise score (if present), referral bonus, interview availability window, notice period, role fit tags.
- Output: a numeric priority score 0–100 and a short reason phrase (2–6 words).

Scoring components (weights):
- Role-match (skills + title alignment): 30%
- Demonstrable impact (projects, OSS, prior product metrics): 25%
- Interview availability & notice period (operational urgency): 15%
- Cultural/mission fit proxies (cover letter, referral, event interactions): 10%
- Screening test / takehome score (where applied): 15%
- Compensation alignment flag: pass/fail (auto-flag for recruiter)

Computation notes:
- Role-match: auto-scored from keyword overlap and hiring manager thumbs-up. If hiring manager marks strong-must-have = +10 to final score (cap at 100).
- Demonstrable impact: map bullet evidence -> 0–25 (scale) using simple heuristics (e.g., shipped feature = 8–15, led infra rollout = 18–25).
- Availability: convert notice period into 0–15 (immediate starts +15, 2–4 weeks +8, >6 weeks 0).
- Screening: if no takehome, treat as neutral (7).
- Compensation: separate boolean; a candidate with compensation mismatch remains in pool but is labeled "comp-mismatch"; recruiter outreach required.

Tiebreaker rules (practical):
- Prefer internal referrals > alumni > cold applicants (referral tag adds +5).
- If still tied, prefer earlier application date.
- Final human check: recruiter reviews top-10 weekly short-list.

Quick example:
- Candidate A: role-match high (27), impact 20, availability 12, screening 13 -> raw=72 -> final=72 + referral 5 = 77
- Candidate B: role-match 30, impact 18, availability 6, screening 13 -> raw=67 -> final=67

2) Interview Rubric (one-page calibration cheat sheet)
- Purpose: reduce subjectivity across interviewers and speed decisioning. Use 1–4 scale (1 = miss, 2 = adequate, 3 = strong, 4 = exceptional) on core dimensions.

Core dimensions (score weight in parentheses):
- Problem solving & algorithms (25%)
- System design / architecture (25%)
- Coding quality & testing (20%)
- Ownership & product sense (15%)
- Communication & collaboration (15%)

Redwood-specific guidance:
- Look for trade-off articulation and SLO/latency considerations for infra/runtime roles.
- For ambiguous answers, probe for past decisions ("tell me about a time when you sacrificed latency for cost or vice versa").
- Document explicit red flags: repeated inability to test-run logic, hostile/entitled behavior, inability to accept feedback.

Decision thresholds (panel):
- Hire now: avg >= 3.3 and no red flags
- Hire with reservations / loop for follow-up: avg 2.7–3.2 with specific gaps identified
- No hire: avg < 2.7 or any single dimension = 1 with behavioral red flag

Interview question bank (starter):
- System design: "Design a request routing layer that prioritizes low-latency inference for VIP customers but guarantees throughput for bulk batch jobs."
- Coding: small kata focused on concurrency or buffer management (30–45 mins).
- Behavioral: "Describe a time you rolled back a production change — what happened and how did you coordinate?"

3) Onboarding Acceleration Kit (30/60/90 condensed with fast checkpoints)
- Aim: get to measurable first-impact (merged PR or runbook completed) within 30 days for IC engineers.
- Fast-lane pre-boarding items (to be completed before day 0):
  - HR forms, payroll setup, laptop request (IT), preread links to infra repo README 
  - Assign a 30-day buddy and first-week schedule with 1:1s booked.
  - Pre-install dev container and credentials; provide a trivial "first change" ticket with step-by-step checklist.

Day 0–7 (orientation + setup):
  - Day 1: manager 1:1 for context, product brief; team onboarding sync; buddy walkthrough of codebase.
  - Day 3: small dev environment smoke test & submit tiny docs tweak PR.
  - Day 7: sync w/ manager to agree on first-impact ticket and success criteria.

Day 8–30 (ramp to first-impact):
  - Week 2: complete paired implementation of first-impact ticket with buddy, automated tests included.
  - Week 3: independent completion + reviewer feedback cycle; demo to team.
  - Day 30: first-impact retrospective: manager + buddy + new hire; capture blockers and celebrate.

30/60/90 success metrics (examples):
  - 30-day: merged PR with tests OR completed runbook + working dev environment verified by buddy.
  - 60-day: 1–2 meaningful features or infra changes with owner-level signoff.
  - 90-day: full ownership of a small service or end-to-end feature.

Manager checklist (fast):
  - Pre-boarding tasks assigned: IT, security, payroll (complete)
  - First-week calendar confirmed (meetings/1:1s)
  - First-impact ticket defined and scoped to 1–2 days of effort for first-change + tests
  - Buddy assigned and objectives communicated

Common ramp blockers (notes):
- No cred or slow IT provisioning: escalate to IT ops with priority tag "new-hire-urgent".
- Overly vague first-ticket: require manager to break into checklist subtasks and ASKS for reviewers.
- Lack of mentorship capacity: consider rotating buddy to ensure distributed load across team.

4) Operational playbook snippets (for recruiters & hiring managers)
- When to use fast-scorer: hiring spike > 3 reqs open for same role, or when >40 CVs in pipeline.
- Escalation: if top-10 scorer candidates not converting after recruiter outreach, loop in hiring manager within 72 hours.
- Compensation negotiation: recruiter files comp-mismatch flag; hiring manager approves counter-offer team budget within 48 hours or candidate is closed.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we expose raw score to hiring managers or only top tier labels? (tradeoffs: transparency vs. over-reliance)
- Integrations: can Greenhouse compute the weighted score? If not, RALLY: quick Google Sheets -> GH import workflow.
- Equity adjustments for diverse slates: include a +bonus to underrepresented cohort hires to account for historical pipeline variance? Need legal review.

Next steps:
- Get feedback from 3 hiring managers (infra, console, devexp) by EOD next Tue.
- Engineering to prototype score calculation in a sheet (Marco) and test on 120 historical applicants (Sofia).
- Draft short training for interviewers (15m async) and distribute with role-specific calibration examples.

Notes to self / shorthand:
- Keep rubric simple — most friction comes from too many axes.
- Focus on operational constraints: notice period and comp alignment matter as much as raw skill in market today.
- Revisit after 2 quarters: measure time-to-offer, time-to-first-impact, and diversity metrics.

End of doc.
